expectations.text: Grounds the priority ranking in the actual current SUOC Platform Registry Fix Now items and real commit/mission history (cites real capability names, risk levels, file paths), not a generic to-do list
expectations.evidence: Cites the same 5 Fix Now items with risk framing and today's real security-remediation commits.

expectations.text: Ranks by leverage/risk with explicit reasoning, not just a flat list
expectations.evidence: 'If I had to pick what to focus on: 1... 2... 3...' with a one-line reason per item — thinner than the with-skill run's explicit leverage framework, but still a reasoned ranking, not a bare list.

expectations.text: Names unresolved ownership/decision gaps explicitly (e.g. TBD-owned capabilities) rather than passing over them silently
expectations.evidence: 'Two areas in the registry — Search and Scheduling — don't have an owner listed (shown as "TBD")... should get assigned to someone.'

notes: This eval doesn't strongly discriminate: a capable baseline independently found the same registry items, the same TBD-ownership gap, and produced a reasoned ranking without the charter's explicit leverage/escalation framework. The with-skill run's edge here is evidentiary hygiene (the stale-commit-hash correction, explicit routing/coordination-status framing) rather than finding something baseline missed entirely.
